status: Selected research design; no baseline, simulator, or training implementation is claimed complete
decision: Adapt published sampled single-step value-of-information planning as the principal non-RL baseline; add transparent project-defined controls and a matched PPO control.

primary_baseline.name: Physical-inspection single-step VOI (adapted)
paper_sections: Section 5.2: EXP and FSSN Single-step VOI
primary_baseline.what_is_reused: Expected-cost comparison and Monte Carlo evaluation under a non-optimal subsequent navigation policy.
what_we_define: Physical inspection viewpoints and visibility constraints
Task budget, timeout cost and observation-miss model
Shared feasible action candidates and training-data-fitted state transitions
original_assumptions: Known graph with initially uncertain edges
Original sensing can query an edge without physically moving to it
Original general-graph policies use an optimistic free-space graph and update it from observations
primary_baseline.adaptation_label: Inspired by and adapted from Bnaya, Felner and Shimony (IJCAI 2009); not an exact reproduction or a new VOI algorithm.
algorithm: Maintain belief state from the agent observation history, never hidden engine truth.

In the initial protocol, changes occur only between tasks. Propagate passage-state change uncertainty at those boundaries, not merely because time passes inside a frozen task. Track task-boundary age separately from physical time since observation.
Generate continue, detour and inspect-viewpoint candidates using the shared candidate generator.
Sample passage-state worlds from the fitted belief model, respecting known observations and the model assumptions.
Estimate cost of each non-inspection action followed by the same fixed reactive continuation policy.

For each inspection candidate, simulate travel to its viewpoint, possible blockages and incidental observations, sensing time, possible missed observations, posterior update, and the same reactive continuation policy.

Average costs across common sampled scenarios. Choose inspection only if its total expected cost beats the best non-inspection choice by the validation-selected margin; otherwise take the best non-inspection action.
Execute only the first candidate in the real environment and replan from actual permitted observations.
primary_baseline.cost_definition: All cost terms use consistent units, such as elapsed simulation seconds plus predeclared timeout/failure penalties. Travel and sensing are included once in inspection-rollout cost, not added twice.
primary_baseline.value_definition: estimated_gain(inspect_e) = min_a E[C(a then reactive continuation) | belief] - E[C(travel to viewpoint, observe, then reactive continuation) | belief].
safeguards: The simulated sensing branch must not teleport the actual agent or reveal remote states.
Reachability checks use the structural/belief map; actual blockage may invalidate an attempted inspection en route.
Missed observations leave uncertainty; they are not evidence that a passage is blocked.
A simple independent-edge belief is a declared approximation, especially under correlated changes and reachability-conditioned task sampling.
Report Monte Carlo sample count, planner latency and tuning budget.
Use a finite task budget and explicit failure cost to prevent infinite continuation rollouts.
primary_baseline.tuning: Select sampling budget and any decision margin on validation scenarios only. Use identical physical task budgets for all methods. Report compute overhead separately.
not_claimed: Optimal handling of correlated hidden passage states

baseline_suite.definition: Keep latest observed passage states and update routes only from permitted contradictory evidence. No discretionary physical inspection.
baseline_suite.caveat: Initially share Dijkstra/A* with other policies; do not label it D* Lite unless that algorithm is actually implemented.

baseline_suite.definition: Validation-tuned age threshold makes relevant entries eligible for rechecking. Use the same candidate viewpoints and planner. Expiration marks uncertainty, not blockage.
baseline_suite.caveat: Recency motivation is literature-grounded, but this particular TTL policy is our defined control, not FreMEn.

baseline_suite.definition: Physical-inspection sampled single-step VOI as specified above.
Discard passage-state history between tasks while retaining known structural layout, then run the shared reactive policy.
baseline_suite.caveat: An adaptation of the reset idea, not a reproduction of EvoNav agents.

baseline_suite.priority: required before attributing gains to proposed features
baseline_suite.definition: Same action interface, training data/budget, seeds and architecture class as proposed PPO, with selected explicit memory-age and route-consequence features masked.
baseline_suite.caveat: A belief feature can encode age indirectly. Report this as an explicit-feature ablation, not complete removal of temporal information. Mask consistently and audit remaining observation channels.

baseline_suite.definition: No discretionary inspection; ordinary local sensing remains enabled.
baseline_suite.caveat: If identical to reactive under the final protocol, report one implementation rather than count duplicate baselines.

baseline_suite.definition: Inspect each eligible unknown/stale passage on the planned route through physical reachable viewpoints, subject to budget.
baseline_suite.caveat: Do not repeatedly inspect a just-confirmed passage indefinitely.

baseline_suite.definition: Planner with current true passage states; labeled privileged and excluded from claims of fair superiority.
baseline_suite.caveat: Oracle observations must never enter normal policies or their candidate generator.

baseline_suite.priority: only when periodic schedules are in scope
baseline_suite.definition: Replace the shared temporal predictor with a licensed FreMEn implementation or explicitly labeled FreMEn-inspired model; hold sensing/planning fixed.
baseline_suite.caveat: Do not call simple age decay FreMEn; do not mistake a predictor improvement for inspection-policy improvement.

proposed_method.algorithm: PPO with compact structured passage candidates
proposed_method.claim: Test whether learned sequential revalidation improves success versus physical cost over competitive sensing/planning alternatives. RL winning is not assumed.
proposed_method.problem_model: Partially observable navigation. A history-derived belief/information state supports control; variable-duration high-level actions yield a semi-Markov decision process. Do not call the partial observation vector the fully observable MDP state.
proposed_method.timing_gate: Before choosing a PPO library, choose fixed-duration decision ticks or implement duration-aware returns/GAE and bootstrap tests. Merely subtracting elapsed time from reward does not correct a constant per-action gamma.

evaluation.seed_note: Proposal target, not a newly verified course minimum. Disclose actual completed independent training seeds; do not relabel evaluation episodes as training seeds.
evaluation.pairing: Evaluate policies on paired scenario seeds; split layouts and temporal patterns into train/validation/test.
evaluation.statistics: Report mean and standard deviation or confidence intervals; resample independent sequences/layouts rather than goals that share memory.
metrics: elapsed simulation time with explicit failure treatment
leakage_tests: Changing an unseen blocked edge must not alter the policy observation before a legitimate observation.
Candidate generation cannot consult live global NavMesh traversability.
Only the labeled oracle can read global passage state.
Changing evaluation seeds must not refit any model or tune thresholds.
unit_sanity_tests: Cost-free perfect sensing can be beneficial; prohibit pointless duplicate checks.
Prohibit inspection above the remaining physical budget.
Static fully known worlds should not pay needless inspection cost.
Known blocked edges and missing observations have distinct semantics.
Terminal versus truncated rollouts and duration discounting must be tested.
